newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. chief phones Zaire's sick leader.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief phones Zaire's sick leader.

text.p: As aid agencies scurry to contain eastern Zaire's crisis, a U.N. spokeswoman revealed on Wednesday that U.N. chief Boutros Boutros-Ghali had managed to speak to ailing Zairean ruler Mobutu Sese Seko in Switzerland.

The Secretary General's spokeswoman at the U.N.'s European headquarters in Geneva, Therese Gastaut, said Boutros-Ghali telephoned Mobutu in the past few days at Lausanne's luxury Beau-Rivage hotel where he is staying.
"It was part of diplomatic efforts. The phone conversation was in the last days -- the last week or so," she told reporters.
She said the two discussed the crisis in eastern Zaire but gave no details of the conversation. Further contact between the two men was not ruled out.
Mobutu has been in Switzerland since undergoing surgery for prostate cancer in August. His prolonged absence has raised fears about the future of his vast, anarchic country if he dies.

Aid agencies would welcome any sign at all that Mobutu is involved in efforts to contain the conflict, which has displaced more than half a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees fleeing fighting between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels.
Mobutu, 66, has not made any public comment on the crisis.
On Tuesday, he sought to reassert his authority in eastern Zaire by placing the eastern provinces of north and south Kivu under military rule with an order sentorders from Switzerland.
It is unclear if Mobutu has the military muscle to win back territory lost to Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire.
The Swiss Foreign Ministry this month extended Mobutu's visa until November 27 on medical grounds. Swiss media reports have said the president required treatment until the end of the year.

Mobutu, who seized power in 1965 after five years of civil war, is one of Africa's longest serving strongmen. He is widely regarded as having used his position for personal enrichment and has some $4 billion in Swiss banks according to Swiss media.
